questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

When I reached home late, I found my children __waiting on me__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **waiting for me**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error here lies in the use of the preposition after the verb "**waiting**."
 
• Replace the preposition "**on**" with "**for**" to correct the sentence.
 
• To '**wait on**' someone means to serve someone.
 
 
• **For example-** *The hotel staff waited on the couple at their wedding dinner.*
 
 
 
• To '**wait for**' something or someone means we are expecting something to happen or we are waiting for someone.
 
 
• **For example-** *When the thieves left the building, the police were waiting for them.*
 
 
 
• "**Waiting for**" is the most common usage when talking about anticipating something or someone.
 
• So, option 4 is the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence:** *When I reached home late, I found my children waiting for m__e.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Our school had decided to take us to the Himalayas for excursion. I ________ to convince my mother to give consent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **left no stones unturned**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank should be filled with the correct idiomatic expression according to the meaning of the sentence.
 
• Let us look at the correct meaning of the given idioms.
 
 
• **Fought fire with fire**: To fight against an opponent by using the same methods or weapons that the opponent uses. (प्रतिद्वंद्वी द्वारा उपयोग किए जाने वाले तरीकों या हथियारों का उपयोग करके प्रतिद्वंद्वी के खिलाफ लड़ने के लिए)
 
• **Brought home the bacon**: To earn the money that is needed to live. (जीने के लिए आवश्यक धन कमाने के लिए)
 
• **Made waves**: To disturb a situation by changing things or by challenging the way things are done. (चीजों को बदलकर या काम करने के तरीके को चुनौती देकर स्थिति को बिगाड़ना)
 
• **Left no stones unturned**: To do everything possible to find some way out. (कोई रास्ता निकालने के लिए हर संभव प्रयास करना)
 
 
 
• ​Therefore, according to the meaning of the given idioms, **option 4** is the correct answer.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: Our school had chosen to transport us on an excursion to the Himalayas. I did everything I could to persuade my mother to agree.

Hence, **option 4** is the correct answer.

**Complete sentence:** *Our school had decided to take us to the Himalayas for excursion. I left no stones unturned__ to convince my mother to give consent.*

questions.question: **Select the sentence with the appropriate use of the adverb of frequency.**

• The adverb of frequency shows how frequently an action takes place.
 
• **Often **is an adverb meaning 'many times on different occasions'.
 
• The adverb "**often**" is commonly used with the simple present tense.
 
• It is used in the front position, in the mid position between the subject and the main verb, after the modal verb or first auxiliary verb, or after being as a main verb or in the end position.
 
 
• **For example-** *I often see Christine when I'm in town.*
 
 
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: Radha frequently visits Nagpur.
 
• So, it is clear that '**often**' implies an action that happens frequently but it is not regular.
 
• Therefore, "**often**" should be used in the sentence.

Hence, the correct sentence with the appropriate use of the adverb of frequency is written in **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

The surgeon says that I should get anaesthesia for the surgery.

options.text: The surgeon says, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”
The surgeon says, “I should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”
The surgeon said, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”
The surgeon says, “You could get anaesthesia for the surgery.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The surgeon says, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is an indirect speech and we need to convert it to a direct speech.
 
• We do not change the tense of the reporting verb if the present simple tense is used for the reported speech i.e. 'says'.
 
• When we change an indirect speech to a direct speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb remains unchanged in the case of a suggestion.
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are placed to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The conjunction "**that**" connects both the clauses of the sentence.
 
• The comma (,) is added after the sentence covered in inverted commas in direct speech.
 
• The first word of the direct speech should be in capital letters.
 
• There should be no changes in the tense in the case of simple present tense.
 
• The 1st person pronoun 'I' changed to the 2nd person pronoun 'you' respectively in the direct speech.
 
 
 
• Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, the direct speech is - *The surgeon says, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”*

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Why is peace being demanded by you?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Why are you demanding peace?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the passive form and we need to change it into the active form.
 
• The given sentence is written in the passive form of the Present Continuous Tense.
 
• The Present Continuous Tense in the passive voice has the following structure: Wh word + am/is/are + object + being + verb 3 + subject +?__
 
• The Present Continuous Tense in the active voice has the following structure: __Wh word + am/is/are + subject + verb (ing) + object +?__
 
• Example - 
 
 
• Passive voice - *Why a song is being sung by Elina?*
 
• Active voice - *Why Elina is singing a song?*
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Passive to Active Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form of the verb.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
 
 
• ​Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct Active Voice: *Why are you demanding peace?*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Not only is my brother intelligent __though hard working__ too.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **but hard working**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace the conjunction "**though**" with "**but**" to correct the sentence.
 
• “**But**” indicates a complete negation and is usually used after a comma, in the middle of a sentence.
 
 
• **For example- ***The food wasn't good, but at least it was cheap.*
 
 
 
• “**Though**” is usually used at the end of a sentence and indicates a partial negation.
 
 
• **For example- ***She seemed healthy, though she is thin.*
 
 
 
• **​**We use "**though**" to introduce a subordinate clause in which you mention something that contrasts with what you are saying in the main clause.
 
• "**But**" is used to add emphasis to a sentence.
 
• The implied meaning of the given sentence is: My sibling is not only smart but also diligent.
 
• Some two-part subjects are joined by “either...or,” “neither...nor,” or “not only...but also.” In these cases, the verb should agree with the subject closest to the verb.
 
• In this sentence, "**not only**" is already mentioned. So, we should use "**but**" according to the subject-verb agreement rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2** which can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

**Corrected sentence:** *Not only is my brother intelligent but __hard working too.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let us look at the use of the other words given in the options.
 
 
• **Or**: Or is a conjunction that connects two or more possibilities or alternatives. It connects words, phrases and clauses which are the same grammatical type.

 
 
• **For example-** *Which do you prefer? Leather or suede?*
 
 
 
• **So**: It is used as a subordinating conjunction to introduce clauses of result or decision.
 
 
• For example- *You are right, of course, so I think we will accept what the bank offers.*
